questions.question: When loading a tank with flammable liquids, what should you do?

options.text: Create a ground connection before opening the filling hole.
Remove the ground connection right before opening the filling hole.
Lock the filling hole during loading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create a ground connection before opening the filling hole.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading a tank with flammable liquids, unless you need to run it for a pump. Create a ground connection before opening the filling hole. Keep the ground connected until after you close the filling hole.

questions.question: What are used to warn others about hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on large packages and on vehicles to warn others about hazardous materials. The shipper is responsible for placing placards. The driver is responsible for checking that the correct placards are in place.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, what else must be shown?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material
The date the product was packed

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material
questions.explanation: If the letter "G" (for "Generic") is written in Column 1 of a shipping paper, the technical name of the hazardous material must also be listed.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be placed when you are driving?
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch in your driver's side door or in another place you can easily reach while wearing your seat belt. The papers must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: If a substance is in a reportable quantity, what letters must appear on the shipping paper and package?
questions.explanation: When hazardous materials are transported in a reportable quantity, the shipper must display the letters "RQ" on the shipping paper and package.

questions.question: Which task is NOT your responsibility at an accident scene?

options.text: Keep people away from the scene
Try to put out a hazardous materials fire yourself
Tell emergency responders about the hazardous materials

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to put out a hazardous materials fire yourself
questions.explanation: Your responsibilities at an accident scene are to keep people away, limit the spread of material if it is safe, tell emergency responders about the dangers, and give them the shipping papers. Do not fight hazardous materials fires unless you have proper equipment and training.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: How fast it must reach its destination

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fall into one of nine hazard classes. The hazard class tells you the dangers of the material.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks while carrying chlorine, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down before crossing the tracks
You can cross without stopping if no warning lights are flashing

questions.explanation: When transporting any amount of chlorine, you must always stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track at a railroad crossing, whether or not a train is coming.

questions.question: Who is responsible for properly labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials properly. The driver should check that the materials are labeled correctly.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained and tested?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials employees must be trained and tested at least once every three years. Training should cover the risks of hazardous materials and how to respond to security threats.

questions.question: If a box contains liquid containers, what must be shown on the box?

options.text: Arrows pointing up to show the correct direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing up to show the correct direction.
questions.explanation: Boxes with liquid containers must have arrows on them. These arrows must point in the correct upright direction.

questions.question: A person watching a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Inside a gas station looking through a window.
Inside the vehicle, awake or asleep.

questions.explanation: A person watching a placarded vehicle must be awake in the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards of the materials, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: What is used to warn people about hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They warn people about the danger.

questions.question: Hazardous materials rules protect everyone except:
questions.explanation: Governments make rules about transporting hazardous materials to protect the driver, people nearby, and the environment.

questions.question: What does "RQ" mean?
questions.explanation: "RQ" stands for reportable quantity. You may write "RQ" instead of "X" on shipping papers to mark a reportable quantity of hazardous material.

questions.question: If cargo catches fire, why should you not open trailer doors?

options.text: Oxygen will enter and make the fire bigger.
It will let in more light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oxygen will enter and make the fire bigger.
questions.explanation: If cargo catches fire, do not open the trailer doors. Opening them gives the fire more oxygen, which makes it grow larger.

questions.question: When carrying explosives, you can leave your vehicle unattended only at:
questions.explanation: A safe haven is an approved location for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives. This is the only place you can leave your vehicle unattended when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: If you find that cargo is leaking, what should you do?

options.text: Touch the material to find out what it is.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the cargo.
Assume all the cargo is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the cargo.
questions.explanation: If cargo is leaking, use shipping papers and labels to identify it. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: The person loading a tank with hazardous materials must do all of the following except:

options.text: Stay within 10 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials.
Be authorized to move the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within 10 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: The supervisor loading or unloading a hazardous materials tank must stay alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet of it, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank.

questions.question: What does Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table show?
questions.explanation: Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table lists the proper shipping names and descriptions of regulated materials.

questions.question: How must containers of hazardous materials be secured?

options.text: Secured so they do not move during transport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so they do not move during transport.
questions.explanation: Containers must be secured so they will not fall, slide, or bounce around while being transported. All hazardous materials packages must be properly secured.

questions.question: Are shipping papers required for hazardous materials?

options.text: No, they are not needed for most shipments.
Yes, they are required for all shipments.
Only if kept in a digital file.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are required for all shipments.
questions.explanation: Shippers must provide proper shipping papers for all hazardous materials. These papers tell others about the risks of the materials.

questions.question: Who is responsible for labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials. The shipper must also provide any required placards.

questions.question: What should you do with the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids?
questions.explanation: You must turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. The only exception is if you need to run the engine to operate a pump.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tires to feel the pressure.

questions.explanation: You must check each tire at the start of every trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only effective way to check if tire pressure is correct.

questions.question: What do you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
Attach a QR code to be scanned.
Make the label smaller to fit on the package.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a label will not fit completely on a package, place the label on a tag that is securely attached to the package instead.

questions.question: On a shipping paper with both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how are the hazardous materials identified?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must be clearly identified on shipping papers that include both hazardous and non-hazardous items. They can be entered first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" before the description.

questions.question: When can an improperly placarded vehicle be moved?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: A vehicle must be properly placarded before driving. An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved if necessary to protect lives or property during an emergency.

questions.question: Which agency helps coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards?

options.text: The United Center for Chemical Assistance

questions.explanation: The National Response Center helps police and firefighters coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards.

questions.question: When do you need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Only in a Class A vehicle.
Only in a Class B vehicle.
Only in a Class C vehicle.
In any vehicle transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: In any vehicle transporting hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials in any sized vehicle.
